**Finding: Compliant** (rule LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer)

The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee payable by the Issuer or Depositor. This satisfies the preferred position outright, so no redline was proposed.

Key points supporting the conclusion:
- **No exit payment on Servicer termination.** Article VII imposes no break fee or make-whole on the Issuer when the Servicer resigns or is removed; instead Cellco must keep performing (§7.3) and automatically assumes the receivables-acquisition obligations under §§2.5/2.6 and the Master Trust RTA (p0316, p0327).
- **Transition costs run against the counterparty.** §7.5(c) requires the resigning or terminated Servicer to pay all reasonable transition expenses of the Issuer, Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and Successor Servicer.
- **§8.3 termination** is purely event-driven (last Receivable paid/written off, or Issuer termination) with no fee.

Two items reviewed and deliberately not flagged:
- The **$150,000 appointment fee / Additional Successor Servicer Fee** (§7.4(c)) is service compensation to a third-party replacement servicer paid from Collections — not a liquidated amount owed to Cellco.
- **Make-Whole Payments** (Article VIII) are noteholder prepayment economics triggered only by a voluntary Optional Redemption elected by the Class A Certificateholder, not a penalty imposed on us.

Payment-shortfall and remittance mechanics in Articles IV and VI impose obligations on Cellco and the Parent Support Provider, i.e. they benefit our side, so they are outside this rule's direction.
